==Question==
Why do particles of the class PA have the consonants they have?
{{mu|no pa re ci vo mu xa ze bi so}}

With vowels it's well known that they follow AEIOU pattern but what about consonants? Why these, not other consonants were chosen?

==Answer==
*[[la lojbab]]:
*#They had to be different from each other.
*#They had to be strongly contrasting against other numerals with the same vowel (hence pa/xa ci/bi and not pa/ba ci/ji or pi/bi).
*#They could not disrupt other paradigms (systems of cmavo) that had good claims to either history or practicality:
*#*{{jvs|ca}}/{{jvs|ba}}/{{jvs|pu}} <> {{jvs|cabna}}/{{jvs|balvi}}/{{jvs|purci}}
*#*{{jvs|da}}/{{jvs|de}}/{{jvs|di}} {{jvs|fa}}/{{jvs|fe}}/{{jvs|fi}}/{{jvs|fo}}/{{jvs|fu}} {{jvs|ri}}/{{jvs|ra}}/{{jvs|ru}} {{jvs|ti}}/{{jvs|ta}}/{{jvs|tu}} {{jvs|vi}}/{{jvs|va}}/{{jvs|vu}} {{jvs|sa}}/{{jvs|si}}/{{jvs|su}} {{jvs|zi}}/{{jvs|za}}/{{jvs|zu}}
*#*{{jvs|ga}}/{{jvs|ge}}/{{jvs|gi}}/{{jvs|go}}/{{jvs|gu}} {{jvs|ja}}/{{jvs|je}}/{{jvs|ji}}/{{jvs|jo}}/{{jvs|ju}} {{jvs|se}}/{{jvs|te}}/{{jvs|ve}}/{{jvs|xe}}
*#*'''lV''' and '''lVV''' used for various sumti classifiers
*#*and a few others
**Once those constraints were set, there weren't all that many contrasting CV choices that also allowed the vowel pattern. Certainly not any that allowed a consonant pattern (as there is with hex digits where the consonants are contrasting <u>and</u> alphabetical). There is a visible trace of an attempt to make them alphabetical {{jvs|no}}/{{jvs|pa}}/{{jvs|re}} {{jvs|vo}} {{jvs|xa}}/{{jvs|ze}} but there were too few uncommitted CVs to make it work.
